title: Kiln-run load harness: benchmarking methodology and customer certification
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a repeatable, tenant-aware load testing harness ("Kiln-run") and a rigorous benchmarking methodology to validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. Deliverables include: the harness code and config templates, an experiment suite for steady-state/ramp/microburst scenarios, autoscaler safety and policy tests, a documented benchmarking methodology for internal signoff, and a customer-facing acceptance checklist + runbook for onboarding Dedicated customers. Goal: reduce onboarding time, provide reproducible evidence for SLA commits, and give engineering a deterministic way to validate fleet-level controls and autoscaler behavior under real-world mixes.
tasks: Design harness architecture: controller, tenant-profiles, traffic generator, result collector
Implement workload profiles: steady-state, ramp-to-steady, microburst, long-tail spike, mixed-models
Integrate with metrics pipeline: expose per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, per-node throughput, queue lengths
Autonomous experiment runner: param sweeps for batch size, seq length, kv-cache warm state
Autoscaler test cases: scale-up latency, scale-down safety window, oscillation prevention checks
Fleet control scenarios: model-fallback routing, region-fallback, reserved-pool contention
Produce a reproducible benchmarking doc and acceptance checklist for Sales/SEs
Add e2e dashboards and alerting playbooks for test regressions and anomalies
Write customer onramp runbook and a short demo script for SOC/solutions engineers
Create a small set of canonical PRs: harness repo, runner, dashboard panels
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a tenant-mix scenario with 200 concurrent tenants and produce deterministic metrics (repeatable within 5% variance)
Benchmark doc contains step-by-step instructions, expected metric ranges for runtime-1.20, and failure modes
Autoscaler policies validated: no oscillation on synthetic microburst tests; scale-up completes within configured SLO
Customer acceptance checklist covers test inputs, run length, expected outputs, and signoff criteria
Dashboards populated: per-tenant QPS, token/sec, tail latency histograms, node-level saturation and GC indicators
Two internal customer pilots executed and signed off by Solutions Engineering with documented test logs
test_plan_summary: Run three classes of experiments: 1) Steady-state sustained for 60m at a target QPS to validate throughput and token-cost; 2) Ramp experiments with configurable ramp durations to validate autoscaler responsiveness and tail latency; 3) Microburst and long-tail spike tests (sub-second spikes and sustained bursts) to exercise KV cache warmup and model-fallback policies. Each experiment will be repeated 3x to quantify variance. Collect token-level telemetry, per-request traces for 5% sampled requests, and resource utilization per GPU pod.
telemetry_requirements: Emit per-request metadata: tenant_id, model_variant, prompt_length, response_tokens
Expose metrics: requests/sec, tokens/sec, decode/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_depth
Aggregate node metrics: GPU utilization, memory pressure, temperature, throttling events
Trace sampling: 5% end-to-end traces linked to a test-run ID
Store raw experiment outputs for 90 days for audit/repro
notes: Trade-offs: we prioritise deterministic repeatability over simulating infinite tenant heterogeneity in initial v1
We will add tenant-level auth simulation in v1.2 to validate multi-tenant isolation effects on autoscaling
Consider adding a lower-overhead tenant-proxy for faster large-scale experiments (future work)
